subject: history_social
passage: Most people picture medieval European castles as great fortresses of stone. ______ many of the first castles built in England after the Norman Conquest of 1066 were made of earth and timber. These motte-and-bailey castles, each a wooden tower set on a mound of earth beside a fenced yard, could be built in just a few weeks.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The first sentence describes the usual image of castles: stone fortresses. The second says many early English castles were made of earth and wood instead. A transition that shows a contrast is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. People's image of stone castles did not cause early castles to be made of wood.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Wooden castles are not an example of stone fortresses; they differ from them.
explanation.C: Correct. "However" signals the contrast between the usual image of stone castles and the earth-and-timber castles described next.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a likeness, but earth and timber differ from stone.
